stories.headline: Justice Department threatens California over noncitizen midterm ballots
stories.note: Trump's DOJ gave California 48 hours to confirm whether possible noncitizens were mailed midterm ballots, threatening emergency court action if the state won't cooperate.
body: The Justice Department is threatening California with emergency court action after saying the state may have mailed midterm ballots to people federal officials believe are noncitizens.

In a Tuesday letter to Secretary of State Shirley Weber, Acting Deputy U.S. Attorney Trent McCotter said federal officials gave Los Angeles County a list of suspected noncitizens and gave the state 48 hours to confirm whether any of them got ballots for the Nov. 3 election. That deadline runs out Thursday.
"If you cannot implement this process by then, given the ongoing federal election, the United States will have no choice but to seek emergency relief," the letter said.

Weber protested, saying Trump and DHS earlier claimed California had 190,000 noncitizens on its rolls without sharing their methodology, and that the DOJ is now demanding the state "blindly trust this administration." She insisted California already bars noncitizens from registering.

The fight sits against a bigger Trump administration push on election integrity. In late September the Supreme Court let states keep using DHS's SAVE system to check voter eligibility while a lower-court ban is on hold.
Why it matters: Republicans get a clear midterm contrast on election integrity as Trump's DOJ presses blue California to scrub possible noncitizen ballots before votes are counted.

stories.headline: Massive trove of Republican voter and donor info breached in Biden DOJ probe: Senate chairman
stories.note: Chuck Grassley says Jack Smith's Arctic Frost probe scooped up personal data on at least 639,000 Republican voters and donors, including MAGA hat buyers' home addresses.
body: Senate Judiciary Chairman Chuck Grassley says a new memo shows former special counsel Jack Smith's Arctic Frost probe vacuumed up personal data on at least 639,000 Republican voters and donors — including people who bought MAGA hats and Trump gear.

According to Grassley, more than 148,000 of those spreadsheet rows were flagged as donors, mostly small-dollar givers. The haul included names, birth dates, home addresses, emails, party registration, jobs, credit-card details and donation amounts.

Smith's team also pulled sales records for red MAGA hats and other Trump merchandise, Grassley said, complete with purchaser names and home shipping addresses — plus a catalog of hats, T-shirts, mugs and door mats shared with FBI agents.

Grassley argues the sweep went far beyond what any special counsel needed and was aimed at "map[ping] out the entire Republican Party apparatus." At a hearing last month, Smith acknowledged gathering donor financial information and said he had a duty to collect facts in a serious criminal probe.

Why it matters: Fresh Grassley evidence that Biden's DOJ invaded ordinary Republican donors' privacy hands the GOP a potent weapon against Democrats' "rule of law" messaging weeks before the midterms.

stories.headline: 9th Circuit blocks California's federal agent ID law in Trump win
stories.note: Even the liberal 9th Circuit sided with Trump, blocking Gavin Newsom's law that forced plainclothes federal agents to show badges during immigration ops.
body: Even the liberal 9th Circuit just handed President Trump a win over California Gov. Gavin Newsom, temporarily blocking a state law that forced plainclothes federal agents to show badges and ID during operations.

The appeals panel said the Trump administration was certain to succeed and that California's No Vigilantes Act identification rule violates the Constitution's supremacy clause by overriding the federal government's power to decide when officers identify themselves.

Newsom has cast himself as a top Trump antagonist on immigration, signing laws meant to restrain federal enforcement. A spokesperson called federal tactics a "campaign of terror"; DOJ officials celebrated, saying California cannot regulate how federal officers do their jobs.

The administration sued in November 2025 over the ID rule and a separate mask ban. A district judge had left the ID requirement in place; the 9th Circuit has now blocked it pending appeal, rejecting California's claim that only substantial burdens on federal ops are unconstitutional.
Why it matters: A court that often fights Trump is telling Newsom he can't micromanage ICE — a legal and political win for federal immigration enforcement heading into November.

stories.headline: Michele Tafoya closes the gap with Flanagan in Minnesota Senate race
stories.note: Fox moved Minnesota's Senate race toward the GOP after a poll put Michele Tafoya within 4 points of Dem Peggy Flanagan as the state's fraud scandal dogs Democrats.
body: Republicans may have a real Minnesota Senate shot: former NFL sideline reporter Michele Tafoya has closed to within four points of Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan in a Star Tribune/KARE 11 poll, and Fox News shifted the race from Likely Democrat to Lean Democrat.

GOP candidates haven't won a Minnesota Senate race in nearly 25 years. Tafoya is running for the open seat of retiring Sen. Tina Smith and is hammering Flanagan over the state's massive welfare-fraud scandal that helped drive Gov. Tim Walz out of his re-election race.

"Walz understood that he was not going to win another term as governor with these conditions, but my opponent thinks she deserves a promotion. I think people are starting to realize she deserves a pink slip," Tafoya told Fox News Digital.

Flanagan says she's "incredibly angry with the fraud" and notes she didn't run the agencies at the center of it. Democrats still call her the favorite and say national GOP talk of flipping Minnesota is a ploy, while Tafoya also pitches a plan against gang violence in the Twin Cities suburbs.
Why it matters: A once-safe blue Senate seat is suddenly competitive as Minnesota's fraud mess sticks to Democrats — a potential pickup that would help Republicans hold the chamber.

stories.headline: NY Rep Mike Lawler clashes with Cait Conley over ICE, sanctuary laws in debate
stories.note: In a pivotal House swing-district debate, GOP Rep. Mike Lawler pressed his Democrat opponent on sanctuary laws after an illegal immigrant accused of killing a teen from his district.
body: In a fiery New York House debate that could help decide House control, GOP Rep. Mike Lawler repeatedly pressed Democrat Cait Conley on sanctuary laws and ICE cooperation less than three weeks from Election Day.

Lawler's suburban 17th District is one of the few swing seats left; he is one of only three House Republicans who won a district Kamala Harris also carried in 2024. Both parties are pouring millions into the race.

The sharpest clash came over immigration. After Conley criticized an ICE shooting involving a man with a child in the car, Lawler noted the man's criminal history and argued New York sanctuary rules stopped local cops from turning him over to ICE earlier.

Lawler then raised Sheridan Gorman, a college student from his district killed in Chicago; the illegal immigrant charged had a prior shoplifting arrest but wasn't handed to ICE under sanctuary policy. "If you think he should have been deported when he was arrested for shoplifting, he should have been turned over to ICE," Lawler said.
Why it matters: A pivotal swing-district Republican put sanctuary Democrats on defense over preventable crime — the kind of contrast House Republicans need in a tough midterm map.

stories.headline: Georgia Senate debate turns ugly as candidates clash over neo-Nazis, Epstein
stories.note: GOP Rep. Mike Collins hit Sen. Jon Ossoff over a million-dollar Epstein-linked donor and refused to let Ossoff's white-supremacy smear define the Georgia Senate race.
body: Georgia's final Senate debate before Nov. 3 turned ugly as Sen. Jon Ossoff accused GOP Rep. Mike Collins of letting neo-Nazi propaganda come out of his own home, and Collins hit back over Ossoff's Epstein-linked megadonor.

Ossoff demanded Collins pledge that no more such material would be produced from his house for the rest of the race, citing reporting on Collins' son-in-law. Collins said he was tired of the attacks, claimed Ossoff's rhetoric had fueled threats against his family, and flipped the script to money.

"You have not denounced, you've not condemned Reid Hoffman, one of your largest donors out there, one that's been supporting you with over $1 million," Collins said. Hoffman, the LinkedIn co-founder, has acknowledged meeting Jeffrey Epstein after Epstein's 2008 conviction and visiting his island; records show $7,000 direct to Ossoff plus $1 million to a supporting PAC.

Collins also tied Ossoff to Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and streamer Hasan Piker, whom Collins blasted for anti-Israel and 9/11 comments. Ossoff's campaign has said he rejects reckless rhetoric, and Collins separately condemned hate speech while saying he has fired staffers over controversies.
Why it matters: Collins refused to play defense-only and put Ossoff's Epstein-tied donor cash and far-left allies on the ballot — a must-watch race for Senate control.

stories.headline: Texas Senate hopeful's pro-border security ad contradicts 2019 interview
stories.note: Progressive Dem James Talarico is running a tough-on-border ad for Texas Senate, but Fox notes he once wanted to strip Texas border funding — a flip-flop Republicans can hammer.
body: Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico is running a tough-on-border ad slamming Joe Biden for failing Americans on the border — but Fox reports he once wanted to wipe out Texas' border-security budget.

In a 2019 Austin Chronicle interview, Talarico called for taking the state's roughly $800 million two-year border-security funding and putting it into public education instead, dismissing boats, planes and Border Patrol as expensive political grandstanding.

His campaign couldn't give Fox an example of him publicly criticizing Biden on the border during Biden's presidency. As a state lawmaker he also called to dismantle ICE, labeled illegal immigrants his constituents, and blasted Gov. Greg Abbott's border policies as atrocities.

Spokesperson JT Ennis now says Talarico has a border agenda endorsed by border-county sheriffs from both parties and supports more Border Patrol plus deporting violent criminals and traffickers. He's running against Attorney General Ken Paxton in a close Texas Senate race.
Why it matters: A progressive Dem reinventing himself as a border-security candidate in deep-red Texas hands Republicans a clear flip-flop to air through Election Day.

stories.headline: FBI probes Long Island Dem party boss after claims he tried to buy votes for reelection
stories.note: The FBI is probing Suffolk County Dem boss Rich Schaffer over insider claims he tried to buy votes to keep his party chair, another black eye for New York Democrats.
body: The FBI is investigating Suffolk County Democratic Party Chairman Rich Schaffer after insiders claimed he tried to buy votes to keep his job, sources told the New York Post.

Schaffer, chairman for 26 years, won reelection last month despite allegations of strong-arming members and offering money for their support against progressive challenger Kathryn Casey Quigley. Several party members and local officials say federal agents have contacted them; the FBI declined to comment.

Accusers describe a pressure campaign that allegedly included threats to jobs and backdoor deals with local Republicans to keep Democrats off the county ballot. Text messages reviewed by the Post show Schaffer discussing payments to get committee members to attend and vote, including asking whether they could "pay him to miss work."

Schaffer called the claims "baseless" and said as of Wednesday he hadn't been contacted by law enforcement. His attorney Mark Lesko called him a "model of professionalism and ethics" and dismissed the allegations as politically motivated. New York's attorney general had already been reviewing whistleblower complaints.
Why it matters: An FBI probe into an entrenched New York Democratic boss over alleged vote-buying is another midterm black eye for Democrats on integrity and machine politics.
